key_impacts: In Fiji, over 60% of the population was affected.
About 22% of Fiji’s housing was destroyed or damaged.
Over 130,000 people were displaced in Fiji.
Approximately 500 schools in Fiji were destroyed.
In Tonga, more than half of the island’s crops were damaged.
missing_information: Exact date range and landfall timing within February 2016.

key_impacts: Affected over 70% of Vanuatu’s population.
Displaced 65,000 people.
Resulted in 11 deaths.
Over 17,000 buildings were damaged or destroyed.
Estimated economic cost was approximately 64% of the country’s GDP.
missing_information: Geographic distribution of impacts within Vanuatu.

key_impacts: Over 6,000 casualties.
Approximately 16 million people affected in over 44 provinces.
Over 4 million people were displaced.
About 1.1 million houses were totally or partially damaged.
In Anguilla, over 90% of electricity and communication services were impaired and almost all roads were impassable.
In Barbuda, over 90% of structures were destroyed.
Barbuda was completely uninhabited for the first time in 300 years following mandatory evacuations.
Mandatory evacuations were ordered for Ragged Island in The Bahamas after complete destruction of infrastructure.
In Cuba, over 150,000 homes were affected along with extensive damages to the electricity grid, communications services and agricultural industry.
missing_information: Full list of all affected territories beyond those named.

key_impacts: In Dominica, 80% of the population sustained damages or destruction to homes.
Telecommunications and electricity were lost for the entire island of Dominica.
In Puerto Rico, the entire island was left without electricity or communications.
Damages in Puerto Rico were estimated at US$30 billion.
missing_information: Sectoral damage details beyond power and telecommunications.

events.event_hazard: Coastal flooding from tropical cyclone (Hurricane Sandy)
key_impacts: An attribution study found the return period of Hurricane Sandy’s flood height in New York City decreased by a factor of three from 1800 to 2000 due to sea-level rise.
missing_information: Damage and casualty figures for New York City.
